newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis sees French Q4 consumer consumption fall.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis sees French Q4 consumer consumption fall.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Tuesday that he expected consumer consumption to fall in the fourth quarter of 1996 but that the trend in spending remained positive.

"We must certainly expect a retreat in the fourth quarter, a statistical backlash from the entirely exceptional level of car sales in the third quarter," he said in a speech to the economic and social council. "But the trend should remain upwards."
In a prepared text released ahead of the speech, Arthuis also said the underlying French economic growth rate would be at least two percent in the second half of 1996.

"Altogether, all the indicators suggest that the underlying trend of activity should attain, in the second half of this year, an annualised rate of at least two percent," he said. "This is of course good news for employment."
Arthuis said he expected the market sector of the French economy to create more than 150,000 jobs in 1997.
"With growth of 2.3 percent, market sector employment should rise by about 160,000 to 190,000 between the end of 1996 and the end of 1997," he said.
The government is forecasting gross domestic product growth in 1997 of 2.3 percent.
